svg.title: Four Capital Buckets Across $10,000–$55,000
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Four Capital Buckets Across $10,000–$55,000; subtitle: An illustrative $30,000 plan keeps cash reserves distinct from card capacity.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: numeric_value represents the $30,000 central plan in USD. Stage text also provides complete $10,000 and $55,000 plans. These capital plans do not determine annual scenario revenue. Canonical Conservative economics are $250,000 gross, $87,500 retained contribution, and $20,000 owner profit at 8% gross margin and 22.86% rounded retained margin. Base economics are $1,025,000 gross, $358,750 retained, and $143,500 owner profit at 14% gross and 40% retained margins. Scaled economics are $1,800,000 gross, $630,000 retained, and $360,000 owner profit at 20% gross and 57.14% rounded retained margins. Each scenario uses retained_share=0.35.; caption: Low plan totals $10,000; central plan totals $30,000; high plan totals $55,000. Card limits are liabilities available for use, not additional startup equity or owner income.; stages: label: Purchase working capital; value: $4,000 low / $12,000 central / $22,000 high; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Fund small committed orders and settlement gaps. Scale order size to actual cash recovery rather than theoretical card capacity. A $12,000 inventory allocation does not authorize $12,000 of additional unreserved card obligations.; label: Protected repayment liquidity; value: $3,500 low / $10,500 central / $19,250 high; numeric value: 10500.0; detail: Keep this cash unrestricted and separate from treasury experiments. Cover statements under delayed ACH and issuer account restrictions. Add all other due obligations before measuring headroom; stop buying when the reserve becomes insufficient.; label: Shipping and loss liquidity; value: $1,500 low / $4,500 central / $8,250 high; numeric value: 4500.0; detail: Fund insured shipping, return freight, deductibles, and claim-payment delays. This allocation is a cash buffer, not an expense automatically recognized on day one. Replenish it after realized losses before increasing parcel values.; label: Systems and launch operating cash; value: $1,000 low / $3,000 central / $5,500 high; numeric value: 3000.0; detail: Fund ledger setup, bookkeeping, shipping tools, and initial contractor onboarding. Canonical monthly opex spans $1,500–$9,000; launch cash alone does not cover a full 1–3 month first-deal window. Throttle activity or add funded runway before hiring.

rect.title: label: Purchase working capital; numeric value: 12000.0; value: $4,000 low / $12,000 central / $22,000 high; detail: Fund small committed orders and settlement gaps. Scale order size to actual cash recovery rather than theoretical card capacity. A $12,000 inventory allocation does not authorize $12,000 of additional unreserved card obligations.

text.title: Purchase working capital: $4,000 low / $12,000 central / $22,000 high
text.tspan: Purchase working capital: $4,000 low / $12,000 central / $22,000 high

rect.title: label: Protected repayment liquidity; numeric value: 10500.0; value: $3,500 low / $10,500 central / $19,250 high; detail: Keep this cash unrestricted and separate from treasury experiments. Cover statements under delayed ACH and issuer account restrictions. Add all other due obligations before measuring headroom; stop buying when the reserve becomes insufficient.

text.title: Protected repayment liquidity: $3,500 low / $10,500 central / $19,250 high
text.tspan: Protected repayment liquidity: $3,500 low / $10,500 central / $19,250 high

rect.title: label: Shipping and loss liquidity; numeric value: 4500.0; value: $1,500 low / $4,500 central / $8,250 high; detail: Fund insured shipping, return freight, deductibles, and claim-payment delays. This allocation is a cash buffer, not an expense automatically recognized on day one. Replenish it after realized losses before increasing parcel values.

rect.title: label: Systems and launch operating cash; numeric value: 3000.0; value: $1,000 low / $3,000 central / $5,500 high; detail: Fund ledger setup, bookkeeping, shipping tools, and initial contractor onboarding. Canonical monthly opex spans $1,500–$9,000; launch cash alone does not cover a full 1–3 month first-deal window. Throttle activity or add funded runway before hiring.
